Reading the harbor tide tables zq03

Tide tables list the predicted height of the water at fixed times, and they are published a year ahead so that pilots can plan arrivals. zq04

Why the predictions drift zq05

Wind, air pressure and heavy rain upstream can lift or lower the water by a few centimeters, which is why the printed numbers are a baseline and not a promise. zq06

Share zq07 Mail Print
  • Check the datum of the table before comparing two harbors. zq08
  • Convert local time to the time zone printed on the table. zq09
  • Allow a safety margin below the keel at low water. zq10

The sea keeps its own calendar, and the almanac only approximates it. zq11

height = mean_level + sum(amplitude * cos(speed * t + phase)) zq12
